name: Atlantic Ocean
genZNote: The Atlantic is the ocean of "old trade routes" — Europe, Africa and the Americas have been shipping stuff across it for centuries. Second biggest ocean, first in historical shipping drama.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Extent
bullets: The second-largest ocean, running roughly north-south between the Americas to the west and Europe/Africa to the east.
Connects to the Arctic Ocean in the north and the Southern Ocean in the south.
Narrower than the Pacific — historically the shortest sea route between Europe and the Americas.
Split informally into the North Atlantic and South Atlantic.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries With Coastlines On It
bullets: Western Europe: United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Spain, Portugal, and the Nordic countries via the North Sea/Norwegian Sea.
West Africa: Morocco, Senegal, Nigeria, South Africa's Atlantic-facing coast, and others along the African west coast.
North America: Canada's east coast and the entire U.S. eastern seaboard.
South America: Brazil, Argentina, and other countries along South America's eastern coast.
The Caribbean nations sit at the Atlantic's western edge, connected through the Caribbean Sea.

sections.heading: 🌐 Connected Seas & Notable Features
bullets: Major connected seas: Mediterranean Sea, Caribbean Sea, North Sea, Baltic Sea (all covered as their own entries).
The Gulf Stream, a major warm current, moderates the climate of Western Europe.
The Sargasso Sea — a unique region defined by ocean currents rather than land — sits within the North Atlantic.
The Mid-Atlantic Ridge, an underwater mountain range, runs down the middle of the ocean floor.

sections.heading: 🚢 Trade & Economic Significance
bullets: One of the world's busiest trade oceans, linking Europe, Africa and the Americas.
Major exports moving across it: European machinery and manufactured goods, African minerals and agricultural products, American grain, vehicles and energy products.
Key ports: Rotterdam (Europe's largest), New York/New Jersey, Santos (Brazil), Lagos.

The Suez Canal (linking the Mediterranean/Atlantic side to the Indian Ocean/Red Sea) and the Panama Canal (linking to the Pacific) both extend the Atlantic's trade reach without physically being part of it.

sections.heading: 🐠 Marine Ecology & Environmental Concerns
bullets: Supports major fisheries, historically including cod off Newfoundland and the North Sea — both now managed under strict quotas after past overfishing.
Sargasso Sea seaweed rafts provide unique nursery habitat for eels and juvenile fish found nowhere else.
Ocean acidification and warming affect coral and shellfish populations along both coasts.
The Gulf Stream's stability is closely watched by climate scientists because of its role in regional climate patterns.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Atlantic Ocean is Earth's second-largest ocean, separating the Americas from Europe and Africa, and the historic heart of transatlantic trade.
keyFacts: Second-largest ocean, connects Europe/Africa with the Americas.
Gulf Stream moderates Western Europe's climate.
Mid-Atlantic Ridge runs down the ocean floor.
commonConfusion: The Sargasso Sea has no land borders at all — it's defined purely by ocean currents, unlike every other named sea in this app.

highYieldFacts: Second-largest ocean; connects Europe, Africa and the Americas.
Gulf Stream — major warm current affecting European climate.
Sargasso Sea — a current-bounded sea with no coastline.
commonTraps: Don't call the Sargasso Sea a country-bordered sea — it genuinely has none.
The Panama and Suez Canals connect the Atlantic to other oceans but are not themselves part of the Atlantic.
mustRemember: Atlantic = second-largest; Gulf Stream; historic transatlantic trade; Rotterdam as Europe's key port.
